branchProtection.verifiedVia: GitHub REST API read-back: GET branches/main/protection and GET rulesets/25523614 after configuration (campaign 079).

ruleset.name: protect main
ruleset.bypassActors: none — current_user_can_bypass: never, so force-push and deletion are blocked even for administrators

branchProtection.adminBypassPolicy: Explicit: administrators bypass the classic rule (required checks do not gate direct pushes by admins) to preserve the repository's autonomous direct-push integration model. Bypass is NOT permission to skip the greenMain local-check rule below, never authorizes force-push of main (the ruleset blocks it for everyone), and must not be used to land a change whose required local checks failed. Emergency force-push/recovery requires explicit owner authorization and a temporary ruleset change that must be restored afterward.
branchProtection.integrationProcedure: Human/normal changes: branch + pull request; the four required checks must pass and the branch must be up to date with main before merge (strict). Autonomous waves: commit to main and push directly after local greenMain checks pass. A rejected push indicates the protection profile changed and must be investigated before any workaround.

greenMain.rule: coherent push to main requires local typecheck and risk-based required checks to pass; a known-failing required check may be pushed only as an explicitly documented blocker/recovery checkpoint, never labeled green.
greenMain.blockedException: only when a required check is EXPECTED to fail (e.g. emulator/AVD gate unavailable in this environment) and the exception is recorded with rationale in the commit/PR and .agent/STATE.md

enforcedGateSet.note: Change 069. Every gate CI actually enforces is declared here, so an UNDECLARED red gate is a detectable contradiction rather than an invisible one. Two gates were red on main while this file named only `typecheck` and `test`; the declaration below is what makes that class of drift self-reporting. Keep in sync with .github/workflows/*.yml — `node scripts/validate-repo-state.mjs` reads this object.
hermeticPushPath: test (jest, enforced via validate-jest-signal + explicit outcome gate)
networkDependentGates: dependency-audit (scripts/validate-dependency-audit.mjs) — needs the npm advisory service; Repository Integrity only. Exit 2 is BLOCKED (did not run), never a pass, and is reported as classification=blocked with the security posture stated UNVERIFIED for that run.

expo-doctor-upstream-drift (npx expo-doctor) — needs https://api.expo.dev/v2/versions/latest; weekly schedule only, tolerated and classified as upstream drift. NOT a repository-defect signal; the hermetic expo-alignment gate is the push-path equivalent.
android-build-smoke / ios-build-smoke (expo prebuild + Gradle/Xcode) — build lanes, not content gates; they need the package registry and (iOS) a macOS host.

notACiGate.expo-doctor-21/21: Never record `Expo Doctor 21/21` as a push-path result. It is network-sourced and time-dependent: it reports upstream patch drift, not a repository state. Record scripts/validate-expo-alignment.mjs instead, with its commit and date.
notACiGate.local-perf-probes: npm run perf:probe runs the 5 bounded perf probes locally; it is not wired into CI and must not be reported as a CI gate.

scheduledOnlyGates: coverage-floors (apps/mobile npm run test:coverage; jest coverageThreshold over db/data-portability/workout/rating/quests) - weekly Repository Integrity job, scheduled-only by decision; floors live in the jest config so any local coverage run enforces them; measurement uses --testTimeout=90000, the push-path matrix keeps 15s
